resources.string: "You know the words. You just never get to speak."
"In a new situation, you don't know what to say"
"What you learn today is gone in a few days"
"Studying every day is easy to plan and hard to keep"
"Each guide explains what the tab is for, then walks through its screen."
"Show each guide again when I open its tab"
"Done. Each tab will open with its guide next time."
"You can see these again anytime in Me → App guide."
"Grammar and vocabulary don't turn into speaking until you actually speak. In front of a native speaker you worry about mistakes, and booking a tutor every day is hard to keep up."
"Here you call yourself: the version of you who already speaks fluently, in a voice cloned from yours. There's no one to be embarrassed in front of, and you can call any time."
"Everything on the Talk page leads to a call."
"A free talk starts right away. Your fluent self speaks first."
"The whole ring is the daily talk goal you set, 10 minutes unless you change it in Me. The coloured part fills as you talk today, and the ring closes when you reach it."
"Scroll down for situations like ordering at a café or a job interview, and for today's news. Tap one and the call starts on that topic."
"Change the language you're practicing, or add another one. Your fluent self speaks it in the same voice."
"The days you studied add up here. Tap it to see your routine and the days behind you."
"Opens Me: your profile, voice, daily goal, plan and this guide. The ring around your picture shows how much of this month's talk time you've used."
"Talk the way you would on the phone. There's no button to hold down."
"When you stop speaking, your fluent self answers. Take your time to think."
"A more natural way to say it"
"Under what you said, you'll see how a native speaker would put it and what to fix. It arrives with the answer, so the conversation keeps going."
"Why words show up at the top"

"These are the words and expressions due for review today. Nobody remembers mid-sentence what they saved last week, so the call keeps them in front of you. Say one in the conversation and it gets a check. A word you've used in a real talk counts as learned and leaves your review. Tap a chip to see what it means and an example."
"When you hang up, the words you used and the sentences you fixed become your own study book in Review."
"Set the call up the way that works for you, even mid-call."
"The slider button next to the mic opens them. The call keeps going while you change things."
"Normal, Relaxed or Slow. It's how fast your fluent self speaks, and it changes from the next thing it says."
"Extra help while you answer. The next page explains it."
"Hide the subtitles, the corrections or the words to use if they distract you. Nothing is lost: your talk's book keeps every correction."
"For when you know what you want to say but can't find the words. It starts out on at A1 and A2."
"Each time your fluent self speaks, a short answer you could give appears above the button, at your level, with its meaning in your language. A blank (___) is where only you know the answer."
"Now and then it asks something you can answer with a word you're studying, and shows you the word. Use it and it gets a check."
"The mistake you make most, like the past tense, is pinned at the top. Your fluent self asks questions that need it, and if the same mistake comes back, its correction is marked."
"A coached call counts as a practice call. Your minutes, streak and book all count, but it isn't used to measure your level, and words you use in it aren't marked as learned."

"A job interview, a call to your landlord, dinner with your partner's parents. You know enough of the language. What you don't know is what to say first, what to ask, and how to get through the awkward moment."
"Watch shows that situation played out by your fluent self, in your voice. You come away with ideas: how to open, what to ask, which expressions work. Then you practice them until they're yours."

"A person you describe once: someone real in your life, someone famous, or someone you invent. Save who they are, how the two of you know each other and how you talk, and they become a character you can bring back."

"What you say depends on who you say it to. Asking for a day off is a different conversation with your boss than with a coworker, and a generic stranger can't show you that difference. With a specific person, every scene sounds like the real thing."

"The more you save about them, the more they sound like themselves. Then put them in any situation and watch the two of you talk it through. One person can be in as many scenes as you like, and the app suggests situations that fit them."
"Decide who it's with and what's happening."
"Tap someone in your people row. Or leave it empty and the scene finds a fitting person for the situation."
"Describe what's coming up in as much detail as you can. Attach a job posting or your CV and it reads them first."
"No time to write? Tap your way down: café, ordering, the order came out wrong."
"Notice how it's done, not just what's said."
"The lines play one after another, and the one playing is outlined. Your lines are in your voice. Watch how it opens, what it asks and how it gets through the tricky part."
"Under every line: shadow it right there, or save it to your expressions."
"The left button plays the scene once more. The right one opens the scene's book in Review, with its words and expressions. Tap the same situation in Watch again for a new take with new ideas."
"An idea is only yours once you've said it."
"Watch the scene and notice the moves you'd never have thought of."
"Save the expressions you want, and shadow the lines."
"The scene's book brings its words and expressions back to you as cards."
"Start a talk from the scene's book: your fluent self plays the other person, and the scene's words wait at the top for you to use. Or tap Say it again to speak your lines from the scene yourself."
"A phrase you heard in a call, a sentence that got corrected. Without seeing them again they fade, and making flashcards yourself takes time nobody has."
"Review fills itself. After every talk and scene, the words, expressions and corrected sentences worth learning are gathered into a book, and come back right before you'd forget them."
"One talk, one book. The newest is on top."
"Every talk and scene you finish becomes one. It's done when you've learned everything inside."
"Words, expressions, shadowing and grammar. Tap one to practice just that part, card by card."
"Everything you've collected from every book, in one place."
"You decide when you see it again."
"Say the word out loud first. Then tap the card to see its meaning and an example."
"Drag the card onto 10 min, Tomorrow or 3 days. It comes back then."
"Drop it on Got it and it stops coming back."
"Best of all, say it in a call: a word you use in a real talk counts as learned. Each week there's also a short test made from that week's own talks."
"The three buttons in the header are about the whole week, not just today."
"Every card you sent to 10 min, Tomorrow or 3 days waits here, in the order it comes back. An orange dot means some are due now."

"When a new week starts, a short report on the last one comes up once: the days you studied, your streak, how long you talked, and what became yours. Every past week stays here, and a dot marks one you haven't opened."

"Once a week, a test made only from that week's own talks: what a word means, the missing phrase, rebuilding a corrected sentence, writing down what you hear, saying a line out loud, and the grammar from your weekly report. A dot means it's open."
"It's hard to keep going when you can't tell whether it's working. And a test score doesn't tell you how well you speak."
"Progress never asks you to sit a test. It measures the words, sentence structures and fluency you actually used in your calls, and shows them as a CEFR level."
"From A1 to C2, measured from what you said."
"Where you are between A1 and C2. The ≈ means it's an estimate, and it gets sharper the more you talk."
"Vocabulary, grammar and fluency each have their own level, with what to work on to reach the next one."
"How much you talked and reviewed over the last two weeks."
"It needs a little of your speech first."
"That's enough of your speech to measure."
"Every call measures again, and when you move up a level, you'll hear about it."
"A plan in your head slips the first busy day."
"Plan your week once here. Each day then shows whether you did it."
"Tap Edit at the top right. Days run across, hours run down."
"Pick what to do there: talk, words, review and more."
"Up and down changes the time, sideways changes the day."
"The same plan comes back every week. Leave a day empty to rest."
"Each date at the top shows how that day went."
"Everything planned for that day is done. Your streak grows by one."
"Any time that day counts. The times are a plan, not a deadline."
"An empty day is a rest day, so it doesn't break your streak."
"What each tab is for, and how to use it"
